[[Providence Park|Civic Stadium]] }} {{1975 Pacific-8 Conference football standings}} The '''1975 Oregon State Beavers football team''' represented [[Oregon State University]] as a member of the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pacific-8 Conference]] (Pac-8) during the [[1975 NCAA Division I football season]]. In their 11th and final year under head coach [[Dee Andros]], the Beavers were compiled an overall record of 1–10 with a mark of 1–6 in conference play, placing seventh in the Pac-10. Oregon State played three home games were played on campus at [[Parker Stadium]] in [[Corvallis, Oregon]] and two at [[Providence Park|Civic Stadium]] in [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]]. Following an eighth straight loss to open the season, Andros announced his resignation in early November, effective at the end of the season.{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=_HkzAAAAIBAJ&sjid=LeADAAAAIBAJ&pg=2677%2C293975 |newspaper=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |last=Conrad |first=John |title=Pumpkin bows out |date=November 2, 1975 |page=1B}} Oregon State's only win came the following week, {{nowrap|7–0}} over [[1975 Washington State Cougars football team|Washington State]] in a [[Land-grant university|land-grant]] cellar matchup in Parker Stadium. {{nowrap|In the season}} finale [[Oregon–Oregon State football rivalry|Civil War]] against [[1975 Oregon Ducks football team|Oregon]] at [[Eugene, Oregon|Eugene]], the Beavers lost for the first time at [[Autzen Stadium]]. Andros stepped down and became the OSU athletic director in late November,{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=EHozAAAAIBAJ&sjid=LeADAAAAIBAJ&pg=5983%2C7794064 |newspaper=Eugene Register-Guard |location=Oregon |title=Beavers find new AD - Dee |date=November 27, 1975 |page=1D }}{{cite news |url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=hPwnAAAAIBAJ&sjid=zfgDAAAAIBAJ&pg=3699%2C3138883 |newspaper=Spokane Daily Chronicle |location=Washington |agency=Associated Press |title=OSU names Dee Andros |date=November 27, 1975 |page=89}} and retired a decade later in 1985. [[Craig Fertig]], a 33-year-old [[1975 USC Trojans football team|USC]] assistant and former Trojan quarterback, was hired as the Beavers' head coach in December, with a three-year contract at $26,000
